A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ElasticTok study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithms and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image/video reconstruction experiments, downstream VQA evaluations, inference-search comparisons and frequency analyses in Section 3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments in Section 4 and adds an encoder-conditioning ablation in Appendix F and reconstruction examples in Appendix G.

M1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 adds an optional variant without encoder mask conditioning, allowing one encoder execution followed by decoder-only token-length search. The principal masking and autoencoding method remains unchanged; expanded descriptions of existing components are documentation additions.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ImageNet, COYO-700M, the custom video collection, and the same downstream image/video VQA coverage, including GQA, POPE, MSVD-QA and MSRVTT-QA. The added ablation and image examples remain within existing tasks and domains.

E2.justification: New Table 5 compares mask-conditioned ElasticTok with a variant without encoder conditioning. The existing fixed-token baselines, quality-matched baseline and four inference-search methods are retained.

E3.justification: New Table 5 controls average token usage when comparing conditioning variants. Appendix G adds reconstruction evaluations at 20 logarithmically spaced token lengths from 256 to 4096. Existing experimental settings are retained; the newly stated binary-search default is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds an ablation testing whether encoder mask conditioning improves reconstruction at matched average token usage. Appendix G extends progressive-reconstruction analysis with four image cases. The earlier context-length, frequency and inference-objective analyses remain.

E5.justification: v2 introduces no new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new ablation uses point estimates, consistent with the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports threshold satisfaction with versus without conditioning: 36% versus 33.1% at 0.001, 79.6% versus 75.3% at 0.003, and 98.5% versus 98.4% at 0.015. Figures 11-14 add qualitative reconstructions. Existing benchmark values and plotted results, including relocated v1 Tables 1-2, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The masking definitions, sampling rule and formal assumptions remain unchanged. The added RingAttention background and tensor-dimension annotations explain existing computations; they introduce no substantive mathematical revision, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: adaptive video tokenization using 2-5x fewer tokens, flexible downstream compute allocation, and selectable inference objectives. Their scientific scope and claimed benefits are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 explains that removing encoder conditioning permits encoder reuse, trading some reconstruction quality for a claimed 2x inference speedup, with desirability depending on downstream model size. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning context length, visual complexity and masking schemes remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents patchify convolutions, LLaMA 2-style autoencoder blocks, mask embeddings, bottleneck projection and the default binary search. Algorithms clarify tensor dimensions, while Appendix E details the existing neural regressor's architecture, 0.003 training target, MSE loss and normalized outputs. Original training and data-curation details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Graves (2016) on adaptive computation and Touvron et al. (2023) for LLaMA 2, and expands explanation of already cited RingAttention. The broader positioning against nested dropout, compression methods and visual tokenizers remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short background section and Appendices E-G, expands technical explanations, annotates pseudocode and updates author, affiliation and conference information. The principal narrative remains largely verbatim, with limited prose editing and relocation of the quality-baseline discussion.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands with four 20-panel reconstruction grids and Table 5. Figure 2 is redrawn to depict encoder-mask inputs, v1 Tables 1-2 move to Appendix F as Tables 3-4, and several retained displays are resized or relocated. Captions also gain explicit FSQ/VAE identification.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through clearer implementation and inference documentation, and its controlled conditioning ablation makes a practical quality-cost tradeoff easier to assess. The expanded examples and revised diagram also help explanation. These gains are limited: central benchmark evidence and claims remain unchanged, and the claimed 2x speedup is not accompanied by timing measurements.
